The incident, the company told the Australian Securities Exchange (ASX), occurred on Friday night and impacted the Lance Project in Wyoming, US.

sources.name: BleepingComputer
excerpts: “On Friday, November 20, Korea Electric Power Corporation (hereafter KEPCO), led by President Kim Dong-cheol, confirmed that some customer information held in its IT systems had been exposed,” the power company states .
KEPCO is South Korea’s main electric power company and a state-controlled, major operator of the country’s critical infrastructure.

Noiem claiming the attack at KEPCO Source: dailysecu South Korea’s Personal Information Protection Commission separately confirmed that KEPCO received an email from a hacker claiming data theft on November 19.
The organization detected the attack on November 20, when it confirmed unauthorized access to its KEPCO ON electricity billing platform and its electronic procurement system (SRM).

A threat actor using the “Noiem” alias has  claimed the attack  and advertised the breach on a hacker forum on November 19, saying that they had KEPCO user data, supplier records, and bidding and contract documents.

sources.name: SecurityWeek
excerpts: South Korean state-owned electric company Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO, KRX: 015760, NYSE: KEP) has disclosed a data breach impacting approximately 1.5 million people.

South Korea’s Personal Information Protection Commission (PIPC) has launched an investigation into the incident, noting that KEPCO received an email from the hacker, verified sample data received from the sender, and confirmed a dark web posting.
The incident, the company says , involved KEPCO ON, its integrated customer service portal, and the supplier relationship management (SRM) platform, which handles procurement and service contracts.

Additionally, the information of 869,761 individuals was stolen from the SRM systems: the names, unique ID numbers, email addresses, and company addresses of 426,827; and the names, affiliation, employee IDs, email addresses, phone numbers, and company phone numbers of 442,934 (including KEPCO staff and partners’ employees).

excerpts: According to a nonpublic advisory, seen by The Register , Microsoft said the attacks, which have already affected two major energy companies , only impact customers on Azure API Management Classic tiers, not Azure API Management v2.

"What they can reach depends on the credential's permissions and whether it is still valid." Norway's National Security Authority (NSM) urged organizations using APIM to assume their secrets and named values had been exposed and rotate all tokens and secrets.
It named gas giant Equinor and hydropower company Skagerak Energi among the affected organizations.

The advisory lists potentially exposed secrets, including named values, client secrets associated with identity providers and OpenID Connect providers, subscription keys, and tokens used to call direct management APIs.
NSM credited Norway's energy sector with first detecting the vulnerability last week.

excerpts: Within the first 24 to 72 hours, procurement and operations teams should verify whether outstanding orders or spare-parts flows rely on Osaki Electric’s affected Japanese facilities and confirm supplier status through established channels, while security teams verify any payment or delivery changes via known contacts and watch for impersonation, unusual remote sessions, and credential changes.

OT-ISAC said that the incident raises concerns about potential delays in smart meter deliveries, equipment replacements, new installations and technical support for utilities dependent on Osaki’s manufacturing operations and regional business network.
The first report identified three Osaki Electric facilities affected by the production shutdown.
The affected sites include its Saitama R&D and Manufacturing Center, Iwate Osaki Electric and Osaki Platech.
Iwate Osaki Electric manufactures product assembly equipment, while Osaki Platech manufactures meter components.

sources.name: The Hacker News
excerpts: What the Update Does and Does Not Remove GL.iNet listed stable security firmware for its router and KVM lines in the security notice it updated today, which now says the update "removes the malware identified in this incident without requiring a factory reset," with settings kept.
The cloud-side fix does not remove malware from devices that were already infected, so owners still need to check their hardware and install the security firmware listed today.
A KVM is a small device used to control a computer remotely as if sitting in front of it.
The company is still investigating whether computers attached to infected KVMs were affected.
It has not said how many devices were infected, when the attacks began, or how its cloud service was breached.

excerpts: Sean Cairncross out as national cyber director | CyberScoop Skip to main content Advertisement Advertise Search Close Search for: Search Advertisement Get our latest cybersecurity news first on Google.
Close Sean Cairncross is leaving his post as national cyber director, CyberScoop has learned.
Cairncross led the Office of the National Cyber Director, which coordinates cybersecurity policy and strategy across the federal government.
A source close to the White House told CyberScoop that President Donald Trump fully supported firing Cairncross from his position as he lacked the strong cyber credentials to perform the job.
His office nevertheless became involved in key administration decisions on AI security and the protection of critical infrastructure.
